about_blocks.text: About Transforming Tides Counselling in Truro

Transforming Tides Counselling is a private outpatient counselling practice in Truro, Nova Scotia. It is not a residential rehab and has no beds, detox or medical care. Clients book sessions at the office on the third floor of 35 Commercial Street in downtown Truro, or meet a therapist online from anywhere in Atlantic Canada.
about_blocks.html: Transforming Tides Counselling is a private outpatient counselling practice in Truro, Nova Scotia. It is not a residential rehab and has no beds, detox or medical care. Clients book sessions at the office on the third floor of 35 Commercial Street in downtown Truro, or meet a therapist online from anywhere in Atlantic Canada.

about_blocks.text: Irene Gunn, a clinical social worker and the practice's owner, started it in 2018 as a virtual service for individuals and couples, partly to get around the long wait lists in the public mental health system. She later added in-person sessions in Truro, and in 2023 the practice became a clinic with several disciplines under one roof. The team now includes a registered psychologist, Dr. Nicole Callan, several counselling therapists, a neurofeedback practitioner and a registered dietitian.

about_blocks.text: Addiction is one of six specialty areas. The addiction therapy page talks about drinking that keeps creeping up, hiding use from family, and trying to quit alone without it sticking. Sessions focus on handling stress without numbing it, talking honestly with the people you love, and managing strong emotions. Dr. Callan, Michelle Smith, Tish Lewis, Irene Gunn and Amber Brewer all list addiction among their areas of focus.

Teens are seen too; most therapists start at 16, and a couple work with younger adolescents.

centre.faq_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Transforming Tides Counselling

faqs.question: Is Transforming Tides Counselling a residential rehab?

answer_blocks.text: No. Transforming Tides Counselling is an outpatient counselling practice in Truro, Nova Scotia. You book sessions in person at 35 Commercial Street or online and go home afterwards. There are no beds, no detox and no medical care, so anyone who needs withdrawal management or live-in treatment should look at Nova Scotia Health services or a residential centre first.

faqs.question: Does Transforming Tides help with addiction?

answer_blocks.text: Yes, through one-on-one counselling. Addiction therapy is one of the practice's six specialty areas, and several clinicians, including psychologist Dr. Nicole Callan and counselling therapists Michelle Smith and Tish Lewis, list addiction among their areas of focus. Sessions work on coping with stress without substances, talking openly with family and managing strong emotions.

faqs.question: What happens on the free consultation call?

answer_blocks.text: The first step is a free phone call of about 20 minutes with the therapist you choose. You briefly share what you want to work on and get a sense of what therapy with them would be like. If it feels right, you book sessions, and the therapist builds a plan with you around your goals.

faqs.question: Where is the office, and how do I get there?

answer_blocks.text: The office is in Suite 305 at 35 Commercial Street in downtown Truro, open by appointment only. Truro is about an hour north of Halifax on Highway 102, around 45 minutes from New Glasgow and about an hour from Amherst. Many clients from farther away use online sessions instead.

answer_blocks.text: Yes. Most therapists see teens from 16, and Mary Robertson and Tish Lewis also work with younger adolescents. Neurofeedback is available from age 8. answer_blocks.text: Neurofeedback is brain-wave training offered in person by Amber Brewer, the practice's neurofeedback practitioner. An assessment measures brain-wave activity, and training sessions then work on the areas that need it. The practice describes it as a medication-free option for ADHD, anxiety, trauma, sleep and focus, and Amber Brewer lists addiction and compulsive behaviour among her areas of focus.
